title: The Signal Grid
instruction: Keep the lockmark to its fixed places, and put a key beside every Signal Grid that codes content.
intro: Democracy has a structure. The lockmark draws it as nine nodes joined by links, with the lever, a larger red node at bottom right, at the place where one change moves the rest. It sits beside the wordmark in the masthead and in a few fixed places, and its drawing never changes.

The Signal Grid uses the same nine nodes to code one thing about a piece: how far a bill has moved, which recurring series it belongs to, or which pillar it serves. A coded grid always sits beside words that say what it shows.

rules.title: Draw the lockmark from its master for its size, and keep its drawing fixed.
rules.rule: The lockmark is a 3 by 3 grid of nodes joined around its edge and through its center, with the lever in signature red at bottom right. Place the 16 px master from 16 to 23 px, the 24 px master from 24 to 47 px and the display master, drawn for our brand guide’s fifth edition, from 48 px.

why.text: At small sizes our fifth edition’s single master lost its shape: at 24 px only 5 percent of its ink was solid, and at 16 px the lever became one pink pixel. The small masters set every node and link on whole pixels and draw the lever one size up, so it still reads as the place where one change moves the rest.

correct.caption: The lockmark’s construction at 240 px, then at true size at 96, 48, 24 and 16 px, and at 48 px on Charcoal and on Prussian.

failure.caption: Our fifth edition’s master scaled to 16 px beside the 16 px master. Its nodes shrink to the width of a link and the lever turns into a single pink pixel.

rules.builders: The lockmark files read --link for the links and --lever for the lever. Leave the lever on the signature token; on Prussian, place the White file. Ask the editor for the display master, which keeps our fifth edition’s drawing.

rules.title: Place the lockmark only in its fixed positions and sizes.
rules.rule: The lockmark appears in four places, once per view: at the bottom right of social cards, covers and posters, 40 px or 0.4 in, inside the margin; beside the wordmark in L3 and L6; beside the section label on report and slide pages, 24 px or 0.25 in; and in a chart legend at 16 px, where chapter 14 calls for it.

why.text: A signature works by turning up in the same place, so a reader finds it without looking. Used as a bullet or scattered as decoration, it stops signing the page.

correct.caption: Two of the fixed places at true size: the bottom-right corner of a report cover, with the lockmark at 40 px inside a 0.5 in margin, and a report page header with the lockmark at 24 px beside the section label.

failure.caption: The lockmark used as list bullets on a flyer, three lockmarks in one view, each one decoration.

specs.label: Anchor
specs.value: Bottom right of social cards, covers and posters; 40 px or 0.4 in, inside the margin

specs.label: Masthead partner
specs.value: Right of the wordmark in L3 and L6, 2.4 cap heights tall

specs.label: Section marker
specs.value: Beside the section label on report and slide pages; 24 px or 0.25 in

specs.label: Legend mark
specs.value: 16 px, in a chart legend, where chapter 14 calls for it

specs.label: Favicon
specs.value: Retired: favicons use ampersand B’s 16 px master (Rule 03.4)

rules.builders: A low-density pattern of the lattice, with no lit nodes, belongs to chapter 12’s patterns and follows its 12 percent ink limit.

rules.title: Set a key beside every Signal Grid that codes content.
rules.rule: A coded grid sits beside words that say what it shows, on the same line or directly under it, at 13 px or larger: the stage and its name for a tracker, the series name for a route, the pillar’s name for a corner. Screen readers get the same words.

why.text: Nine dots at 24 or 40 px cannot explain themselves, and our fifth edition’s grids coded six things with no words nearby. With the words beside it, the grid becomes a shortcut for readers who know it and hides nothing from readers who do not.

correct.caption: A tracker row at true size: the grid at 40 px beside its key, “Stage 4 of 9: Out of committee”.

failure.caption: The same row with the grid alone. Four filled nodes sit beside the bill’s name with nothing to say what they count.

specs.label: Key
specs.value: On the grid’s line or directly under it

specs.label: Size
specs.value: 13 px or larger

specs.label: Screen readers
specs.value: The grid is hidden; the key’s words carry it

rules.builders: Write the key from the record’s data, so the words and the grid can never disagree, and mark the grid aria-hidden="true" when the key sits beside it.

rules.title: Let each grid code one thing, chosen in this order: tracker progress, a series route, a pillar corner.
rules.rule: When a piece could carry more than one code, its grid shows the first that applies. Progress may add the stage where a reader can take part now, and a series route always ends on its pillar’s corner. A pillar corner shares its grid with nothing else. Content type is never coded by color; name it in words in the kicker.

why.text: Our fifth edition’s grid coded pillar, content type, progress, gaps and series on the same nine nodes, and a reader could not tell which one was in front of them. Its four content-type colors look alike in grayscale, and its Verdigris and red differ at 1.14 to 1. One code per grid, chosen in a fixed order, gives every grid one meaning.

correct.caption: The three codes at 40 px, each with its key: progress, a series route and a pillar corner.

failure.caption: Our fifth edition’s content-type grids in color and in grayscale. Prussian, Verdigris, Charcoal and red collapse into four grays.

specs.label: Order
specs.value: Tracker progress, then a series route, then a pillar corner

specs.label: Tracker progress
specs.value: From 40 px

specs.label: Series route and pillar corner
specs.value: From 24 px

specs.label: Content type
specs.value: In words, in the kicker

rules.builders: The composer after Rule 08.9 builds only the combinations this rule allows.

rules.title: Show tracker progress with a shape for each stage, from 40 px.
rules.rule: A tracker grid reads its nine stages left to right and top to bottom. A filled disc marks a stage done; a ring marks the stage under way; a gap, with the node and its links cut away, marks a stage that never happened; a small Stone node marks a stage not yet reached. One red disc may mark the stage where a reader can take part now. Name each stage in plain words, and say once on each tracker page what each stage means.

why.text: Shapes survive grayscale, color blindness and a cheap printer, and plain stage names let a newcomer read the key. Our fifth edition told the stage under way from a finished one by color alone, Verdigris against red at 1.14 to 1, and drew a missed stage as a dashed ring, a texture the atlas gives to a plausible link.

correct.caption: A tracker list at true size, first at a phone’s 358 px and then at 600 px: four bills, each grid beside its stage in words, a legend of the shapes and a line on what each stage means.

failure.caption: Our fifth edition’s Active and Ready grids at its 28 px tracker size and enlarged four times, in color and in grayscale. In gray the two states are the same picture.

specs.value: Centers at 3.5, 19.5 and 35.5 px; 1 px links

specs.label: Done
specs.value: 7 px disc

specs.label: Under way

rules.builders: Give the red disc to the stage only while the reader can act, and only when no error holds the view’s red (Rule 05.3).

rules.title: Give each recurring series one fixed route that ends on its pillar’s corner.
rules.rule: A series route runs along the links, never across a diagonal, and ends on the corner of the pillar the series serves. Six series hold six routes, and a new series takes a route no other series uses.

why.text: A route lets a regular reader spot a series at a glance, and ending on the pillar’s corner ties each series to the pillar order: Explain top left, Track top right, Connect bottom left, Act bottom right.

correct.caption: Six series and their six routes at 40 and 24 px, each beside its name.

failure.caption: A seventh series drawn with a diagonal from the center to a corner. The lattice has no diagonal link, so the route reads as a break in the grid.

specs.label: Route
specs.value: A 3 px line along the links

specs.label: Nodes on the route
specs.value: 5 px discs

specs.label: End
specs.value: A 7 px disc on the pillar’s corner

specs.label: Smallest size
specs.value: 24 px

rules.builders: List a new series with its route in the table before it ships, and check that no other series holds the same nodes in the same order.

rules.title: Light one corner to name a pillar, and print the pillar’s name beside it.
rules.rule: The four corners follow the pillar order in reading order: Explain top left, Track top right, Connect bottom left, Act bottom right. Light one corner as a 7 px disc at 24 px, keep the other nodes small and Stone, and set the pillar’s name beside the grid.

why.text: The pillars run Explain, Track, Connect, Act, and the corners take them in the order a page is read. Under 48 px a pillar mark sits with its word, and the corner follows the same rule.

correct.caption: The four pillar corners at 24 px, each beside its pillar’s name.

failure.caption: A 16 px grid with every node the same size and one in Verdigris for Track, in color and in grayscale, at true size and enlarged. In gray nothing is lit.

specs.label: Lit corner
specs.value: 7 px disc at 24 px

specs.label: Other nodes
specs.value: 3 px, Stone

specs.label: Smallest size
specs.value: 24 px, with the pillar’s name

rules.builders: Use a pillar corner only where the piece belongs to no series; a series route already ends on its pillar’s corner.

rules.title: Build the kicker from a 24 px grid, a 24 px icon and a label.
rules.rule: The kicker, the short line above a title, sets the grid at 24 px, 12 px of space, a Civic Line topic icon at 24 px in one color, 12 px, then its words in the label style at 13 px. The words follow Rule 01.21: the content label, then after a middle dot the series name if the piece belongs to a series, or else the topic. A record’s ID, when there is one, follows as a typed chip.

why.text: One definition keeps every kicker the same height and order on the site, in email and in reports. Our fifth edition defined it twice, with 20 to 24 px grids and labels at 10 and 11 px, under the 13 px floor.
why.basis: Our 13 px floor for text; Design judgment

correct.caption: The top of a story card at true size: the Dispatch route, a public meeting icon, the words “Report · Dispatch” and the bill’s ID, over the headline.

failure.caption: Our fifth edition’s kicker, with a 16 px grid and 11 px labels. The grid turns to specks and the labels fall under the floor.

specs.value: 24 px, a series route or a pillar corner

specs.label: Space
specs.value: 12 px between parts

specs.label: Icon
specs.value: Civic Line at 24 px, one color

specs.label: Words

rules.builders: Let the kicker wrap after the label; the grid and the icon stay together on the first line.

rules.title: Keep every grid state still, and say it in words.
rules.rule: Empty, loading, ready, under way and final each have their own drawing and a line of text. Nothing pulses: loading shows the links alone, with the words “Loading tracker” in a status region that screen readers announce.

why.text: Our fifth edition pulsed the lever between 20 and 50 percent opacity with no end and no pause, at 1.27 to 1.83 to 1 on Newsprint. That fails WCAG’s rules on moving content and on contrast for graphics, and the pulse told a reader nothing a word could not.

correct.caption: The five states at 40 px with their words, on Newsprint, Charcoal and Prussian.

failure.caption: Two frames of our fifth edition’s loading state at 28 px and enlarged four times, with the lever at 20 and 50 percent. Neither frame reaches 3:1.

specs.label: Empty

specs.label: Loading

specs.label: Ready
specs.value: Stages done as filled discs; the stage in words

specs.label: Under way
specs.value: A ring on the current stage

specs.label: Final
specs.value: All nine filled

specs.label: Motion

rules.builders: Put the state’s words in an element with role="status" and change only its text, so a screen reader announces each change once.

sources: “Democracy has a structure.” is the lockmark’s explanatory line, approved by Dustin Cathcart in October 2026.
